paper_sections.title: Glucose metabolism and serotonin receptors in the frontotemporal lobe degeneration
Positron Emission Tomography Data Analysis and Statistics
Calculation of [11C]MDL100,907 Positron Emission Tomography Binding Images

description.value: The study examined whether apathetic and disinhibited behavioral syndromes in the frontal variant of frontotemporal lobar degeneration are associated with distinct patterns of cerebral glucose hypometabolism, and assessed in vivo 5-HT2A receptor density using PET.

design.value: A cross-sectional PET study of 18 patients with the frontal variant of frontotemporal lobar degeneration, classified into apathetic and disinhibited behavioral syndromes, with comparisons against healthy control subjects. 18F-FDG PET was performed in all patients and 24 age-matched healthy controls; [11C]MDL100,907 PET was performed in 8 patients and 6 healthy volunteers.

description.value: A total of 18 fv-FTLD patients; all were right-handed.

medical_condition.value: frontal variant of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (fv-FTLD)

clinical_characteristics.value: Signs or symptoms of their disease appeared 6 to 72 months (mean, 28 months; median, 22 months) before this evaluation. Disease severity ranged from 1 to 3 according to a clinical classification.

description.value: Twelve patients (six men and six women) showed apathetic behavioral patterns. The apathetic behavioral syndrome was characterized by executive deficits, ideomotor slowness, apathy and indifference, lack of drive and emotional reactivity, and poor language output.

clinical_characteristics.value: Apathetic patients were older, less educated, and more severely affected in instrumental activities of daily living than disinhibited patients.

description.value: Six patients (all men) demonstrated disinhibited behavioral patterns. The disinhibited behavioral syndrome was characterized by mild executive deficits, relentlessness, disinhibited behavior, emotional lability, lack of concern for others, impulsiveness, perseveration, and utilization behavior.

clinical_characteristics.value: Disinhibited patients were younger, more educated, and less severely affected in instrumental activities of daily living than apathetic patients.

description.value: Twenty-four age-matched healthy control subjects underwent 18FDG PET.
Eight of 18 fv-FTLD patients were recruited for the [11C]MDL100,907 studies; five were apathetic and three were disinhibited, and none of the patients was depressed.

medical_condition.value: frontal variant of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (fv-FTLD)

clinical_characteristics.value: Five of the patients were apathetic, three were disinhibited, and none of the patients was depressed. Hamilton Depression Scale scores had a mean of 4.6 ± 2.39 and a range of 1-8.

description.value: Six healthy volunteers were recruited for the [11C]MDL100,907 studies.

task_description.value: 18FDG and PET were used to study the 18 fv-FTLD patients and 24 age-matched healthy control subjects in resting state, with eyes closed and ears unplugged, after intravenous injection.

stimuli.value: No task stimuli; subjects were scanned in resting state with eyes closed and ears unplugged.

task_description.value: The in vivo expression of 5-HT2A receptors was performed using [11C]MDL100,907 as a tracer.

instrument.value: GE Advance PET scanner (GE-Advance; General Electric Medical Systems, Milwaukee, WI)

description.value: A transmission scan lasting 10 minutes was started 40 minutes after tracer injection and was followed by a three-dimensional static emission scan that lasted 15 minutes. Intravenous injection was 185 to 296 MBq.
